roleNote: An example of what you can build from kit components. Start from it, change it, or ignore it; layout is your choice. Follow `must` (kit look and accessibility); `defaults` are this example's suggestions, change any of them.
copyNote: Not exported from agentic-ds-kit. add copies the source into your app (components/patterns/app-shell/) with this contract beside it. You own the copy: replace the demo data, rearrange or drop sections, and keep the `must` lines.
intent: One layout option, as a copy-in example: AppHeader over SideNav + content when wide (>= --grid-breakpoint-md, 64rem; layout-shell / layout-app, radius none, no gap), in a flat or inset look. The wide rail collapses to icons (labels in tooltips, remembered for the browser session); a props nav can carry a Projects group and an account menu at the bottom; an optional right work panel holds Tabs. Narrow, the SideNav moves into a left Drawer opened by a Menu Button at the start of AppHeader, and the work panel opens in a right Drawer. header is optional: without it the shell is side nav only when wide (SideNav shows its brand header and toggle) and a minimal top bar (narrowHeader) holds the Menu Button only when narrow. Top bar only, side nav only, or neither are equally fine: compose AppHeader, SideNav, and Drawer yourself.
useWhen: A product app needs persistent chrome: a top bar, a side nav, or both, that adapts to small screens
The nav should collapse to an icon rail to give the page more room
Pages need a secondary panel of details or activity beside the main content
doNotUseWhen: A single focused task with no app chrome (sign-in, onboarding) — use the sign-in or onboarding pattern
A temporary side task over the page — use kit Drawer on its own
Docs or catalog navigation — use AppNav

header.note: Optional. Omit it for side nav only when wide: no top bar, the shell is one row (layout-app fills it) and a SideNav props nav shows its brand header (showHeader true; a built nav reads useAppShell().hasHeader). Below the breakpoint narrowHeader shows so the Menu Button has a home. Otherwise AppHeader props except radius (always none); the shell builds the start region: when wide, logo or mark in the brand cell, title, then the rail toggle at the open rail's edge; when narrow, the Menu Button in the brand cell, then the logo or mark and title. Use logo for a real logo (keep it within --space-8; --space-6 reads smaller than the letter mark). Known gap: a start slot replaces the whole brand cell, logo included, so a props header with start loses the injected Menu Button; put AppShellPattern.MenuButton inside your start (or build the header from compose parts). Or a header node built from AppHeader.Root and its compose parts: then the shell injects nothing and the header must place AppShellPattern.MenuButton (usually as the AppHeader.Brand logo).

narrowHeader.note: Header-less shells only (ignored when header is set): the top bar shown below the breakpoint, where the nav lives in the Drawer. AppHeader props (the shell injects the Menu Button in the logo slot, radius none) or a built header that places AppShellPattern.MenuButton. Default: AppHeader titled navLabel or nav.title with the Menu Button in the brand cell, then markIcon or mark beside the title (the shell's own mark / markIcon props, else a SideNav props nav's when it sets one), and no search, so the brand shows on narrow screens too. The nav's default letter mark is not repeated: set mark or markIcon to show it.

nav.note: SideNav props except showHeader, radius, and side: title, mark or markIcon, groups or items, footer, open / defaultOpen / onOpenChange for the wide rail. The Drawer shows the same data, always expanded, titled nav.title. Or a nav node you built (a SideNav preset, or SideNavRoot with SideNavNav / SideNavSection / SideNavItem and the other compose parts): the shell renders it in the rail when wide and inside the Drawer when narrow; it reads useAppShell().navPlacement to adapt (showHeader false; radius none in the rail; in the Drawer kit SideNav fills it with no rail width or frame and is always open on its own). Or a function (placement: rail | drawer) => node, so a nav that takes a placement prop (ShellNav from add side-nav) needs no hook.

navLabel.note: Drawer title on narrow screens. Default nav.title, or Navigation for a built nav.

layout.note: flat: the rail sits on a soft neutral fill (--sidenav-background surface-muted), the page runs edge to edge, hairline dividers (border-faint). inset: layout-shell--inset; the nav and top bar share the page background (bg-canvas) and the page column sits in a raised card (radius-surface-lg, shadow-xs) with a small margin.

collapsed.note: Controlled rail collapse, wide screens only: the rail shrinks to icons (--sidenav-width-collapsed) and every row names itself in a kit Tooltip. Without it the shell keeps the state itself and remembers it in sessionStorage for the browser session. A props nav's open / onOpenChange still work and win over the stored state. Ignored when narrow (the Drawer is always expanded).

defaultCollapsed.note: Uncontrolled start state when nothing is stored yet for this session. The server render and first paint use it, so hydration matches; a stored value applies right after.

onCollapsedChange.note: (collapsed: boolean) => void. Fires from the rail toggle (header shells) or the SideNav Toggle / mark (header-less shells).

projects.shape: { label?: string (default Projects), items: SideNavItemData[], newLabel?: string (default New project), onNew?: () => void }
projects.note: Props nav only. Adds a captioned group after the nav groups (a flat items list becomes the first, uncaptioned group). Keep the list short. With onNew, the last row is a Plus row named newLabel. A built nav adds its own SideNavSection.

account.shape: { name: string, email?: string, src?: string, initials?: string, menu: DropdownMenuGroup[], onSelect?: (id: string) => void, menuLabel?: string (default Account menu) }
account.note: Props nav only. Last in the nav footer, below footer rows: SideNav.Account (Avatar sm, name, email) with an icon-only kit DropdownMenu (ChevronsUpDown, align end) holding menu, e.g. Settings, a Theme submenu, Sign out. The menu opens above the trigger when there is no room below. On the collapsed rail only the avatar shows (name in a Tooltip) and the menu trigger is removed; expand the rail to reach it. Replaces nav.account.

workPanel.shape: { title: string, tabs: TabItem[] (min 2), open?: boolean, defaultOpen?: boolean (default false), onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void, tab?: string, defaultTab?: string, onTabChange?: (id: string) => void }
workPanel.note: Optional right work panel, off by default. Wide: an aside named title, fixed at --layout-rail beside the page with a hairline start border, a close Button (X, Close <title>) and kit Tabs size sm. Narrow: the same Tabs in a right kit Drawer titled title. A props header gets a PanelToggle at the start of its actions (unless it sets end); otherwise place AppShellPattern.PanelToggle yourself. Fixed width only; resizing is not offered (kit Resizable is a framed card, not chrome).

mark.note: Brand letter or node for the default narrowHeader, beside the title. Set it (or markIcon) when nav is a built node or a function: the shell cannot read a mark from those, so without it the narrow top bar shows the Menu Button and title only. When neither mark nor markIcon is set here, a SideNav props nav lends its own. Ignored by a custom narrowHeader, when header is set, and when wide (a built nav shows its own brand).

markIcon.note: Icon mark for the default narrowHeader: a Lucide name (e.g. "Receipt"), a Lucide component, or an element. Wins over mark. Same fallback and scope as mark.

children.note: Page content: a layout-canvas or layout-workspace, or another pattern. Pages own their one primary Button. A layout-canvas defaults to layout-header (title row) + layout-content (padded, scrolling stack) inside; content put straight into the canvas is padded and stacked by the canvas.

className.note: Extra class on the layout-shell root, e.g. layout-shell--viewport (layout.css) to fill the viewport height (100dvh, 100vh fallback) with no app CSS; the page then scrolls inside the canvas. Zero the body margin (a CSS reset does).

customChrome.note: header and nav accept nodes built from kit compose parts. The shell keeps the layout (layout-shell over layout-app, no gap), the breakpoint, and the Drawer.

exports.AppShellPattern.MenuButton: Also AppShellMenuButton (use the named export from Server Components). Exported from your app-shell copy. Tertiary sm Menu Button that opens the nav Drawer when narrow; renders its children when wide (e.g. <AppHeader.Mark>A</AppHeader.Mark>). Focus returns to it when the Drawer closes. ariaLabel default Open navigation.
exports.useAppShell(): Exported from your app-shell copy. Inside the shell: { narrow, navOpen, openNav, closeNav, navPlacement: rail | drawer | null, hasHeader, collapsed, setCollapsed, railId, hasPanel, panelOpen, setPanelOpen, panelId }. A built nav reads collapsed and passes open={!collapsed} to SideNavRoot in the rail. Null outside AppShellPattern. Client components only.
exports.AppShellPattern.RailToggle: Also AppShellRailToggle. Tertiary sm Button (PanelLeftClose / PanelLeftOpen) that collapses and expands the wide rail; aria-expanded and aria-controls point at the rail; label Collapse sidebar / Expand sidebar. Renders its children when narrow. A props header gets it after the logo or mark and title, at the end of a brand row as wide as the open rail (--sidenav-width), so it lines up with the nav's edge; a built header places it after its AppHeader.Brand.
exports.AppShellPattern.PanelToggle: Also AppShellPanelToggle. Tertiary sm Button (PanelRightOpen / PanelRightClose) with aria-expanded that shows and hides the work panel; ariaLabel default Work panel. Renders nothing without workPanel. Focus returns to it when the panel's close Button is used.

rules: A built header must contain AppShellPattern.MenuButton; without it the shell warns and narrow screens cannot reach the nav
Put the Menu Button in AppHeader.Brand's logo so it sits on the rail axis, as the preset does
A built nav is one landmark (SideNav preset or SideNavRoot + compose parts); the same node moves between rail and Drawer, it is never rendered twice
Build the nav from the named block exports (SideNavRoot, SideNavSlot, SideNavNav, SideNavSection, SideNavItem, SideNavFooter): they work from Server Components, where SideNav.Root dot access does not

In the shell, drop SideNavHeader and SideNavToggle when there is a top bar (AppHeader has the brand and the Menu Button); with no header, show the brand in the rail when useAppShell().hasHeader is false; in the Drawer force the nav open (open, or inDrawer || open) so it is never a closed rail
A props header that sets start loses the injected Menu Button: place AppShellPattern.MenuButton inside your start
In the Drawer, radius md; leaf picks close the Drawer, disclosures (aria-expanded) do not
A built nav follows useAppShell().collapsed in the rail (open={!collapsed}) and stays open in the Drawer
A built header that wants collapse places AppShellPattern.RailToggle after its AppHeader.Brand (the logo stays in the brand cell); AppShellPattern.MenuButton keeps the brand cell when narrow
customChrome.snippet:
<AppShellPattern
  header={
    <AppHeader.Root ariaLabel="Acme">
      <AppHeader.Brand logo={<AppShellPattern.MenuButton><AppHeader.Mark>A</AppHeader.Mark></AppShellPattern.MenuButton>}>
        <AppHeader.Title>Acme</AppHeader.Title>
      </AppHeader.Brand>
      <AppHeader.Search placeholder="Search" onSearch={setQuery} />
      <AppHeader.Actions><Avatar name="Maya Chen" size="sm" /></AppHeader.Actions>
    </AppHeader.Root>
  }
  nav={<MyNav />}
  navLabel="Acme"
>
  …
</AppShellPattern>
customChrome.copyIn: npx agentic-ds-kit add app-header and add side-nav copy ShellHeader (AppHeader compose parts) and ShellNav (SideNavRoot / Nav / Section / Item / Footer compose parts). Both import only kit components and work without app-shell. To host them here (in a client component): header={<ShellHeader menuButton={AppShellMenuButton} />} nav={(placement) => <ShellNav placement={placement} />}.

responsive.breakpoint: --grid-breakpoint-md (64rem). matchMedia reads the token at runtime; AppShellPattern.css repeats 64rem only for the first paint before hydration.
narrow: No SideNav in the layout; content takes the full width
With no header, narrowHeader (default a minimal AppHeader titled like the nav, with the shell's mark or markIcon, else a props nav's, when set) appears only here, to hold the Menu Button
Menu Button (tertiary sm, lucide Menu, ariaLabel "Open navigation") sits in AppHeader's start column
Left Drawer size sm holds SideNav showHeader false, always expanded
Picking a leaf, Escape, or a scrim click closes the Drawer; focus returns to the Menu Button
AppHeader search stays an Input; below 38rem AppHeader already stacks it under the brand row
Widening past the breakpoint closes the Drawer and brings SideNav back without a reload
The work panel moves into a right Drawer (size md) opened by AppShellPattern.PanelToggle; the rail toggle hides
The 64rem switch follows the token; there is no separate 900px step

requirements: Menu Button is a kit Button with ariaLabel "Open navigation"
The Drawer is the kit dialog: aria-modal, focus trapped, Escape and scrim close, focus restored to the trigger
Parent nav items (disclosures) do not close the Drawer; leaves do
Active leaf keeps aria-current=page in both SideNav and the Drawer
With a built header, AppShellPattern.MenuButton is the only Drawer trigger; it carries the same label and focus return as the injected one
Landmarks: AppHeader is the banner header, SideNav is the nav (inside an aside), page content sits in <main>, the work panel is an aside named by its title
Rail toggle, Menu Button and PanelToggle are kit Buttons with aria-expanded; the rail toggle and PanelToggle also set aria-controls
Collapsed rail: every row and the account avatar name themselves in a kit Tooltip on hover and focus; labels stay in the DOM
Both Drawers (nav, work panel) trap focus, close on Escape and scrim click, and return focus to their trigger
The work panel close Button is named Close <title> and returns focus to the PanelToggle when there is one
The account menu is a kit DropdownMenu: aria-haspopup=menu, arrow keys, Escape closes it and returns focus to its trigger without closing a parent Drawer

must: Semantic tokens only (agentic-ds-kit/tokens.css); no raw hex, no primitive --color-* ramps
At most one appearance="solid" mode="primary" Button per view; the shell has none, pages own theirs
Do not restyle kit components; change them through their props, slots, and tokens

Render inside a main landmark (wrap the pattern, or your page content, in <main>); header and nav chrome, if any, use AppHeader / SideNav (or other header / nav landmarks) and nav stays reachable on small screens
Overlays are kit Drawer or Modal (focus trap, Escape, scrim, focus return built in); no local scrim, sheet, or fixed overlay, and SideNav itself is never an overlay
Breakpoints follow --grid-breakpoint-md: matchMedia reads the token; media queries cannot read var(), so CSS repeats 64rem with a comment naming the token
A custom header places AppShellMenuButton (accessible name and focus return built in); without it narrow screens cannot reach the nav
defaults: layout flat; the rail expanded; the work panel closed
Narrow screens: the nav moves into a left kit Drawer behind a Menu Button; another pattern is fine as long as the nav stays reachable
The Menu Button sits at the start of AppHeader, in the brand cell on the rail axis
Below the breakpoint there is no fixed SideNav or collapsed rail; the Drawer holds the nav
Chrome is layout-shell (AppHeader, radius none) over layout-app (SideNav, radius none, no header), no gap
Without header: side nav only when wide (SideNav brand header on), top bar only when narrow
layout-shell--viewport on className when the shell is the whole page
One layout option among many: top bar only, side nav only, both, or neither are all fine
Collapse is remembered in sessionStorage (key agentic-ds-kit:app-shell:collapsed) for the browser session
headerlessSnippet: <AppShellPattern className="layout-shell--viewport" nav={{ title: "Acme", markIcon: "Receipt", items, footer }}><main className="layout-canvas">…</main></AppShellPattern>
snippet:
<AppShellPattern
  className="layout-shell--viewport"
  layout="inset"
  header={{ title: "Acme", mark: "A", onSearch: setQuery }}
  nav={{ title: "Acme", items }}
  projects={{ items: projects, onNew: createProject }}
  account={{ name: "Rin Okafor", email: "rin@example.com", menu: accountMenu, onSelect }}
  workPanel={{ title: "Context", tabs: [{ id: "details", label: "Details", content: details }, { id: "activity", label: "Activity", content: activity }] }}
>
  <main className="layout-canvas">…</main>
</AppShellPattern>
doNot: Do not hand-build a sidebar, rail, account card, or tab strip; use SideNav, SideNav.Account, DropdownMenu and Tabs
Do not add layout values outside the closed enum (flat, inset); restyle through tokens and component cssVars instead
Do not open the work panel by default; it is opt-in (defaultOpen or open)
Do not keep a collapsed rail below the breakpoint; the Drawer holds the nav there
Do not hard-code a breakpoint other than --grid-breakpoint-md (64rem)
Do not put a second solid primary Button in the chrome; pages own their one primary action
Do not use a local scrim, sheet, or fixed overlay for the nav or the work panel; use kit Drawer
